identity.variant: three-color triangular boundary; executable d=3 and d=5 paper patches

card.description: A self-dual CSS family cut from the square-octagon tiling. Data qubits sit at vertices; every colored face supplies an X check and a Z check on the same vertices. In the bulk, one square and two octagons meet at each qubit. The finite code is not fixed by that bulk label: this entry chooses a disc with one boundary of each color and ships the two small triangular incidences that can be audited directly against the cited paper figures.

views.description: The constructor expands every selected face boundary into one binary row and uses the same row space for X and Z checks. Their stacked symplectic generator matrix is the executable baseline for commutation, rank, and logical calculations.

Red square faces have four vertices and blue/green bulk octagons have eight. Boundary truncation turns some octagons into four-vertex checks. The constructor makes the face-incidence matrix once and uses it for both HX and HZ, so commutation reduces to the even overlap of any two face boundaries.

Dualize the patch so colored face checks become vertices and data qubits become cells. Removing one color class at a time gives ordinary matching graphs; decoding solves those projections and then reconciles them into one color-code correction. The boundary nodes belong to the graph definition rather than an after-the-fact matching option.

Under perfect-syndrome bit-flip noise, one data-qubit error couples the three colored checks meeting at that vertex. Maximum-likelihood decoding therefore maps to a disordered three-body spin model, making the three-way syndrome correlation explicit instead of replacing it by three independent pairings.

A bounded-depth local Clifford transformation maps color-code degrees of freedom to surface-code sectors on derived lattices. This is an equivalence dictionary useful for decoding and phase comparison, not a claim that the square-octagon checks or triangular boundaries are literally surface-code checks.

A connected same-Pauli string along any colored side commutes with every face because each incident check meets it evenly. On this three-boundary disc the three side representatives differ by stabilizers and encode one logical pair, rather than one logical qubit per side.

origin.converter: constructor boundary incidence and GF(2) row-space checks

params.distance: Code distance for an executable, paper-audited triangular patch. The current constructor accepts only 3 and 5; it rejects larger odd distances rather than inferring their incidence from a bulk formula.
params.boundary: Exact finite-patch convention. The supported literal is 'three-color-triangle'; closed, punctured, and other planar boundaries are distinct variants.

decoders.noise: code-capacity Pauli noise with perfect syndrome on a triangular 4.8.8 patch whose three colored boundaries are included in each projection
decoders.notes: Graphical or restriction decoding turns the colored syndrome into surface-code-like matching subproblems and then lifts their union back to a color-code correction. The projections are correlated, so solving them as unrelated graphs loses information; no threshold is attached here without the source's lattice, channel, and lifting rule.

decoders.noise: repeated noisy syndrome extraction on triangular 4.8.8 patches, with spacelike data faults and timelike measurement faults derived from a specified measurement circuit
decoders.notes: Each restricted graph is extended through time before matching. A circuit-level graph must include correlations introduced by the weight-four and weight-eight extraction circuits; a threshold for one schedule is not a schedule-independent property of this check matrix.

realizations.description: The experiment encoded both the smallest triangular block and a distance-five seventeen-data-qubit block, then ran a multi-block logical magic-state-distillation protocol. Its published distance-five face incidence is the qubit order used by this constructor; the experimental result is a protocol claim with postselection and hardware-specific gates, not a growing-distance memory threshold.

A two-dimensional nearest-neighbour architecture specifies syndrome extraction and logical Clifford mechanisms on square-octagon patches. It is a circuit proposal rather than a hardware demonstration.

relations.how: This entry fixes the 4.8.8 bulk tiling and one explicit triangular three-color boundary convention inside the wider family of two- dimensional color codes on trivalent, face-three-colorable cellulations. The parent target is pending as a separate Atlas entry.

The 4.8.8 and 6.6.6 tilings realize the same two-dimensional color-code order, while their face weights, finite boundary staircases, qubit counts, extraction circuits, and decoder graphs remain different.

Local Clifford unfolding produces surface-code sectors on derived lattices. With boundaries those sectors can remain attached along a fold, so this relation is a representation map rather than the direct constructor recipe for the shipped incidence matrices.

operations.cost: one parallel physical-H layer; it exchanges the identical X and Z face incidence matrices and swaps the declared logical X/Z boundary strings
one parallel physical phase layer with S/S-dagger selected by the bipartition; the induced logical convention must be tracked for the chosen boundary basis
one pairwise physical-CNOT layer between corresponding qubits; geometric alignment, transport, syndrome extraction, and correlated recovery are additional resources
compatible colored boundaries, an ancillary region, repeated joint checks, decoding, and feed-forward; the logical action depends on the complete merge/split protocol

operations.gate: non-Clifford gate by magic-state injection or distillation
operations.cost: encoded resource blocks, transversal inter-block Clifford operations, stabilizer/factory postselection or correction, measurement, and classical feed-forward
